newsitem.title: USA: Ore., Enron working to settle merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Ore., Enron working to settle merger pact.

text.p: Talks between staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC), Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co on terms for the companies' planned merger were continuing, a spokesman for the commission said late Wednesday.
He said the tone of the negotiations - which have centered on the amount of a rate cut for Oregon electricity customers - had improved from the morning session.
"Both sides returned to the bargaining table. It looks like Enron came here to close this deal - I think that's what they are working on right now," spokesman Mike Allegre said.
Enron's most recent offer was for an overall rate cut of $61 million, while the OPUC staff was seeking $105 million, an analyst at the commission said Tuesday.
Allegre said Wednesday no information was available on specific changes in those terms during the afternoon session of the settlement meeting.
"There will probably be no final word until tomorrow," he added.
